𝗔𝗻𝗱 𝘆𝗲𝘁 𝗱𝗶𝗿𝗲𝗰𝘁 𝗶𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗸𝗲𝗽𝘁 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗴. 𝗨𝗦𝗗 𝟱𝟳 𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻 was realised in the first half, half of it foreign, and FDI grew 𝟮𝟳% year on year in the third quarter.
Portfolio money reacts to headlines. This year even gold, the classic safe haven, fell more than 𝟮𝟬% from its January record in a matter of days. Direct investment, the kind that builds hotels, factories and jobs, looks twenty years ahead. The real question is where it goes, and what it builds.

Tourism already generates 𝟰.𝟴% 𝗼𝗳 𝗜𝗻𝗱𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗮'𝘀 𝗚𝗗𝗣. That's more than palm oil (around 3.5%) and about twice real estate (around 2.4%). Only mining, oil and gas included, is clearly bigger, at 8.8%, and it shrank last year. Yet tourism receives 𝗹𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝗻 𝟰% 𝗼𝗳 𝗻𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗶𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁, and around three quarters of that still lands in Jakarta and Bali. The government's target is for tourism to reach 𝟴% 𝗼𝗳 𝗚𝗗𝗣 𝗯𝘆 𝟮𝟬𝟰𝟱.

One caution: tourism investment grew 𝟭𝟲.𝟲% in the first half, while international arrivals grew only 𝟱.𝟳%. Capital is arriving 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗲𝗲 𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲𝘀 𝗳𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿 than foreign visitors. Underwrite accordingly, and price the currency: revenue comes in rupiah, even when expectations are set in dollars.

→ 𝗪𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲 exactly to deploy?
→ 𝗪𝗵𝗶𝗰𝗵 𝗮𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘁 𝗰𝗹𝗮𝘀𝘀, 𝘀𝗲𝗴𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴?
→ 𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗳𝗶𝗴𝘂𝗿𝗲𝘀 are really being underwritten?
→ What is the 𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗸-𝗮𝗱𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗿𝗲𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗻, not just the headline IRR?

→ Who 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗹𝘀 it, and how do you 𝗲𝘅𝗶𝘁?

In Indonesia, most of those answers must be decided before the day the company is incorporated.

Stock never matches. Cash drawers come up short without a trace. And existing POS systems are either too expensive, overly complex, or locked to proprietary hardware.

→Immutable Inventory Ledger: Built with an append-only stock ledger, goods receipts, wastage tracking, and 3-step inter-branch transfers so digital stock always matches physical reality.

Functional beverages are entering a more specific phase of innovation. 

Consumer interest is moving beyond general energy boosts towards more targeted benefits, from focus and mood support to sustained energy throughout the day.

One development worth watching is Zynamite®, a mango leaf extract being studied as a non-stimulant ingredient for cognitive performance. Its potential applications point to an interesting opportunity for F&B brands: exploring functional propositions that don't rely entirely on caffeine.

For product developers, this opens up new formulation possibilities. A beverage designed around focus or cognitive support could appeal to consumers looking for alternatives to conventional energy drinks, or simply a different way to support their daily routines.

But the commercial opportunity depends on a few practical questions. 
Is this benefit relevant to a clearly defined consumer group? 
Does the ingredient work within a formulation that delivers on taste, texture, and stability? 
And can the final product justify its price point while communicating its benefits credibly?

Clinical research can make an ingredient interesting. 
Building a product around it requires a much deeper understanding of consumer needs, formulation constraints, and the market it intends to serve.

The real opportunity lies in translating ingredient innovation into a product that earns a place in consumers' everyday habits.

🎤 Speaker announcement: Reifa T. 🇮🇩

"I Automated Myself."

In early 2025, a CTO made AI mandatory across every team. Reifa made it work for QA: AI for test planning, AI-assisted automation, documentation generated straight from Jira.

It worked. Within a year, developers were running the tests themselves, documentation was automated, and UI/UX had absorbed the manual checks.

Then she was moved to frontend development, and the QA team was quietly reduced.

The lesson? AI didn't replace testing. Execution got automated, but judgement, deciding whether software is safe enough to release, had never been claimed.

At taqelah! Testing Conference 2027, Reifa shares the playbook she wishes she'd had, with four practices you can start next week:
✅ Sort your week into execution, systems thinking and judgement, and see honestly how much AI could already take
✅ Automate your own execution work first, on your terms
✅ Make your judgement visible with a short release risk note managers and developers can act on
✅ Treat community as career infrastructure

No tools to buy. Just a different way to show what testers are for.

Reifa is CEO and Co-Founder of SQUADAP, a QA consulting and ISTQB training company in Indonesia. She co-founded ISQA, Indonesia's largest QA community with 9,000+ members, and is Co-Founder and VP of IDSTB, Indonesia's ISTQB and TMMi board. I joined APRIL in 2018 to better understand how water moves through peatlands. Today, I lead the operational water management planning team, working with hydrologists, engineers, surveyors and field staff. Our work ranges from managing water tables to assessing seasonal flood risk across peatland and mineral soil landscapes.

One of the most rewarding parts of my job has been mentoring and coaching staff. When we sit down to review results, I ask four questions.
What happened?
Why did it happen?
Why does it matter?
What should we do next?

I enjoy seeing someone gain the confidence to explain what their findings mean for the people working in the field and make a recommendation they’re prepared to stand behind.

I’m grateful to the colleagues I’ve worked with over these eight years, especially the field teams whose observations have often changed how I understood a problem.

Data Center Power Infrastructure and Clean Energy Procurement in Indonesia: Engineering Hypothetical-Grade Reliability and Bankable Supply

As digital transformation, cloud adoption, and artificial intelligence accelerate across Indonesia—led by strategic hubs in Batam, Greater Jakarta, and emerging regional corridors—data center operators face a non-negotiable infrastructure requirement: near-zero downtime paired with credible low-carbon power. 

Yet from an energy investment origination and enterprise risk governance perspective, hyperscale and enterprise data centers introduce acute load-profile and commercial challenges.

Institutional investors, infrastructure funds, and tier-one EPC partners deploy capital only when ultra-high availability, grid resilience, and bankable clean-energy structures are engineered together.

Powering next-generation digital infrastructure in Indonesia requires aligning utility-scale generation, storage, and distribution with strict digital uptime standards.

Six core pillars define bankable data center energy infrastructure in Indonesia:

 1. Tier-III/IV Redundancy & N+1/2N Power Architecture: Data centers cannot tolerate micro-sags, voltage dips, or brief outages. Bankable designs integrate dual-feed utility substations, fast-response backup generation, and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) for seamless ride-through.

 2. Ramped Load Phasing & Substation Capacity Alignment: Digital campuses scale in phased MW blocks rather than instant peak draw. Aligning phased power-delivery schedules, transformer capacity, and take-or-pay ramp clauses protects both developers and power suppliers.

 3. 24/7 Clean Firming Beyond Intermittent Solar: Because data centers operate continuously, daytime solar alone is insufficient. Combining renewable generation with BESS, hydro, geothermal, or firm grid supply delivers credible round-the-clock decarbonization.

 4. Transparent Tariff & Wheeling / REC Governance: Bankable commercial structures clarify power pricing formulas, transmission or distribution wheeling rules, and auditable Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) or green-attribute accounting for global enterprise tenants.

 5. Tropical Cooling Efficiency & Industrial Water Security: High ambient heat and humidity drive substantial cooling loads. Pairing power infrastructure with high-efficiency cooling, closed-loop water systems, and reliable water supply safeguards operating costs.

 6. Physical Security, Cyber-Physical Resilience & ABAC/ESG Standards: Strict site access controls, supply-chain security, anti-bribery and anti-corruption (ABAC) compliance, and transparent ESG reporting satisfy global cloud and institutional underwriting standards.
